sentences.text:
ORAL ORDER Mr Dhaval M. Barot, learned advocate for the petitioners states that the subject matter of challenge,
is the order dated 10.02.2023 which, has been passed on the premise that the petitioners, are not possessing licenses under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Gujarat Shops and Establishment (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2019.

entities.text: Gujarat Shops and Establishment (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. It is submitted that so far as license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is concerned,
the petitioners possess it with a validity upto 24.03.2025; so far as the license under the Gujarat Shops and Establishment (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2019, is concerned, if the employees engaged are more than 10, then license is required, but if the employees, are less than 10, only intimation, is the requirement.
3.

entities.text: Gujarat Shops and Establishment (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted that the petitioners, shall file an application before the authorities concerned with all the requisite documents and the authorities, may decide the same in accordance with law.

To which, Mr Kamlesh S. Kotai, learned advocate for the respondent - Nagarpalika states that if application is made by the petitioners with requisite documents, the respondent shall take a decision Mahmad Salim Ansari vs Mehsana Nagarpalika on 7 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96103792/
1 in accordance with law.

Let the respondent - Nagarpalika, take a decision, strictly in accordance with law, preferably within a period of four weeks' from today.
6. With the aforesaid direction, the petition stands disposed of.
7. It will be open to the petitioners, to approach this Court in case of difficulty.

8. Direct service is permitted.
